summary: Executed frontend-only SEO regression on public URL for route-wise metadata, canonical tags, JSON-LD, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and runtime stability after react-helmet-async integration.

integration_issues.issue: Duplicate meta description tags are rendered on each route: a static description from public/index.html plus route-level Helmet description. Automated SEO validators may read the wrong one and Google snippet control becomes inconsistent.

action_items: Remove static SEO description/keywords/OG/Twitter tags from frontend/public/index.html (or keep only non-conflicting defaults) so route-level Helmet tags are single-source-of-truth.
Re-run SEO checks to ensure exactly one meta description per route and correct per-route content is exposed to crawlers.
critical_code_review_comments: RCA: index.html still contains hardcoded SEO meta tags while react-helmet-async injects route tags, causing duplicate metadata in the final head. This is why title updates pass but description checks read stale default content depending on selector/crawler behavior.
Canonical implementation is correct route-wise and JSON-LD School schema is present on home only (as intended).
No frontend runtime break observed from react-helmet-async in tested routes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated on https://educational-hub-5.preview.emergentagent.com across /, /about-us, /academics, /activities, /gallery, /disclosure, /contact-us. Titles and canonicals are correct on all tested routes; robots.txt and sitemap.xml are accessible and include expected directives/URLs. Main remaining blocker is duplicate description metadata from index.html + Helmet.
rca of the issue: Repro: open any route and inspect document head. Two meta[name='description'] tags appear. First is global default from index.html, second is route-specific from SEOHead. Mitigation: keep only one meta description source, preferably Helmet-managed route tags; then revalidate with crawler-like checks.
